title: Microburst stall absorber and adaptive admission policy
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: We observe brief microburst traffic patterns that cause single-digit-millisecond spikes at p99+ for prefill->decode handoffs. Root cause analysis shows: (1) sudden admission of long-prefill requests overwhelms kernel slots; (2) attention-cache prewarm misses create decode stalls; (3) current kernel selector is slow to pick a lower-latency kernel for short sequences, causing head-of-line latency amplification.

Goal: Implement a runtime component (Microburst Stall Absorber) that combines an adaptive admission policy, micro-sliced batch shaping, and fast kernel-fallback hints to reduce p99/p999 latencies during microbursts without materially reducing aggregate throughput. Target: reduce p99 by >=25% and p999 by >=30% for mixed traffic traces from customer workloads while keeping throughput loss <=5%.

Proposed design:
- Admission: add a microburst detector based on moving-window packet arrival entropy and slot utilization. When a microburst is detected, switch to an aggressive admission profile that temporarily raises per-tenant prefill acceptance thresholds and enables per-request short-horizon token pacing (10-50ms windows).
- Batch shaping: introduce micro-slicing that favors many small batches over fewer large ones during detected microbursts. Batches are shaped to maintain efficient kernel packing while preventing decode queue build-up. Use a cost heuristic: minimize expected tail latency = alpha * p99_est + beta * throughput_delta.
- Kernel hinting: augment request metadata with a fast-kernel hint generated from a light-weight sequence-length and attention-sparsity estimator at enqueue time. The admission controller propagates the hint to the kernel selector which can bypass full profiling for small sequences, immediately selecting lower-latency kernels (e.g., fused attention or reduced KV-window engines).
- Attention prewarm: opportunistically prefetch attention KV blocks for requests in the admission short-horizon to reduce first-decode miss penalty. This uses evictable prefetch slots guarded by a budget meter to avoid cache thrash.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype microburst detector in serving proxy (flags only, no behavior) and run in shadow for 2 weeks on canary region. (Diego)
2) Implement adaptive admission state machine and micro-slicing in scheduler runtime (Ava).
3) Add kernel-hint metadata field and fast estimator (small C++ module in enqueue path).
4) Integrate attention prewarm budget and LRU-evict mechanism in KV cache layer.
5) End-to-end tests + synthetic microburst replay harness (replay tool + production traces).
6) Gradual rollout: shadow -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metric gates.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive admission reduces bursts but may increase average latency for long-running batches; mitigate via time-limited state and hysteresis.
- Attention prewarming improves first-decode but increases memory churn; enforce strict budget and measure eviction rates.
- Kernel hinting simplifies selection cost but risks suboptimal kernel choice; collect fallback telemetry and auto-tune alpha/beta heuristics.

Metrics & dashboards:
- Primary: p95/p99/p999 for prefill-to-decode tail, decode stall rate, first-decode latency.
- Secondary: overall throughput (tokens/sec), kernel-utilization, KV cache hit rate, prefetch eviction rate, per-tenant acceptance delta.
- Dashboard links: https://dashboard.internal.redwood/runtime/microburst (dashboard stub), experiment logs: gs://redwood-experiments/microburst/2026-02.
comments: 2026-02-12 Diego Morales: Created ticket after analyzing customer trace set (2026-01-redwood-mixed-traffic). Noticed recurring sub-100ms spikes at p999 during traffic bursts. Attached initial analysis and histogram. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/microburst-analysis-2026-02

2026-02-20 Ava Chen: Implemented prototype microburst detector in proxy. Running shadow mode in us-west1. Initial detection rate matches expected microburst windows in 12/15 production traces. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4512

2026-02-25 SRE review (Priya Kapoor): Concern about prefetch budget interacting with eviction under memory pressure. Suggested adding soft limits per-GPU and circuit-breaker to avoid OOM. Action: add budget meter and circuit-breaker (Ava).

2026-03-03 Diego Morales: Kernel hint prototype added; lightweight estimator uses sequence-length percentiles + attention-sparsity sketch. Microbenchmark: kernel selection latency reduced from 0.85ms -> 0.18ms for short sequences. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4870

2026-03-06 Ava Chen: Began implementing micro-slicing in scheduler. Early synthetic runs show tail p99 reduction ~18% on mixed trace, throughput drop ~2.3%. Need further tuning of alpha/beta cost weights. Added experiment configs in gs://redwood-experiments/microburst/config-v1.json

2026-03-10 PM feedback (Lena Hart): Emphasize gradual rollout gating and customer opt-in for Dedicated customers. Added acceptance criteria and gating thresholds. Linking product note: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Microburst+Mitigation+Plan

2026-03-12 Ava Chen: Updated ticket with integration blockers: (1) kernel-selector API requires a small change to accept hint enums; (2) existing A/B rollout infra needs metric gate for p999. Created sub-issue ENG-907655 to track selector API change.
acceptance_criteria:
1) On canary traffic, with microburst mitigation enabled, prefill->decode p99 decrease >=25% and p999 decrease >=30% relative to baseline deck.
2) End-to-end throughput change <=5% on 12 production traces.
3) No memory OOMs attributable to attention prewarm (prefetch eviction rate < 3% after budget enforcement).
4) Fallback telemetry shows kernel-hint fallback rate < 5% after 1 week of canary.
5) Rollout plan and gating documented in Confluence and approved by SRE and PM.
